advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the `--check` flag actually gate the non-zero exit (or drop the flag and document the always-fail behavior).
evidence: scripts/check_docs_index.py:105: `    parser.parse_args(argv)` — return value discarded, no `args.check` reference
scripts/check_docs_index.py:116: `    return 1 if (unindexed or broken) else 0` — unconditional on the flag
Running `python scripts/check_docs_index.py` without `--check` would also exit non-zero on findings, contradicting the flag's documented purpose
advisory.finding: The `--check` CLI flag is parsed but its value is never used; `main()` always returns 1 whenever there are findings regardless of whether `--check` was passed, making the flag a no-op and its help text ('exit non-zero if there are unindexed docs or broken links') misleading.
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture `args = parser.parse_args(argv)` and only return non-zero when `args.check`; otherwise just report. Or remove the flag and document that the script always fails on findings.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the stale 'STUB'/'held-out TDD loop' wording from the module docstring now that the checker is fully implemented.
evidence: scripts/check_docs_index.py:2: `"""Docs-index completeness / dead-link checker (ticket f088) — STUB.`
scripts/check_docs_index.py:4: `API contract (implemented by the held-out TDD loop):`
Functions find_unindexed/find_broken_links/main are all fully implemented below
advisory.finding: The module docstring labels the file a 'STUB' whose API contract is 'implemented by the held-out TDD loop', but the file is fully implemented; the header is stale and misleading to future maintainers.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the docstring header with a description of the shipped behavior (index completeness + docs-internal broken-link checks).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit allowlist for designated historical/archive docs as required by the ticket AC (or confirm the AC is satisfied because such docs are already indexed).
evidence: scripts/check_docs_index.py:57: `        if md.match("*.local.md"):` — only allowlist rule
Ticket AC: 'The allowlist covers *.local.md and designated historical/archive docs.'
find_unindexed only globs top-level `docs/*.md` (line 53), so any future top-level historical doc that is intentionally unindexed would fail with no exemption path
advisory.finding: Ticket f088 AC states the allowlist must cover '*.local.md AND designated historical/archive docs', but only `*.local.md` is implemented; there is no mechanism to exempt an intentionally-unindexed top-level historical doc. Currently benign because existing historical docs are indexed and archive docs live in a subdir not scanned, but the AC requirement is unmet.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strip an optional trailing markdown link title (`"..."` / `'...'`) from parsed link targets so titled links parse correctly.
evidence: scripts/check_docs_index.py:25: `_LINK_RE = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)]+)\)")`
A link like `[x](file.md "Title")` yields target `file.md "Title"`, which won't match `file.md` for indexing nor resolve as a path
search of docs/README.md for `.md "` returned no matches, so not currently triggered
advisory.finding: The link-target regex `\]\(([^)]+)\)` does not handle markdown links with titles (`[t](url "title")`) or targets containing parentheses; it captures the trailing title as part of the target, which would cause both find_unindexed and find_broken_links to mis-parse such links. No such links exist in the current docs, so this is latent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the archive/historical-doc allowlist required by ticket f088 (currently only *.local.md is handled and no test covers archive docs).
evidence: Ticket f088 AC: 'The allowlist covers *.local.md and designated historical/archive docs.'
scripts/check_docs_index.py:57 `if md.match("*.local.md"):` is the ONLY allowlist branch
grep for 'archive' in scripts/check_docs_index.py returned no matches
docs/archive/ exists with tier-e-execution-plan.md, README.md — real archive docs the ticket references
ABSENCE: no test in test_check_docs_index.py exercises an archive/historical allowlist entry
advisory.finding: No test covers the archive/historical-doc allowlist behavior required by the ticket AC ('The allowlist covers *.local.md and designated historical/archive docs'). The implementation only allowlists *.local.md and has no archive handling, so a doc under docs/archive/ (or a designated historical top-level doc) is neither implemented nor guarded by a test.
scenarios: A historical/archive doc is added and the gate either wrongly flags it or the archive-allowlist requirement is silently dropped

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a broken-link test with a .md in a docs/ subdirectory to cover rglob recursion and parent-relative (md.parent) link resolution.
evidence: scripts/check_docs_index.py:73 `for md in sorted(docs_dir.rglob("*.md")):`
scripts/check_docs_index.py:83 `resolved = (md.parent / path_part).resolve()`
docs/ contains subdirectories adr/, archive/, design/ each holding .md files
ABSENCE: _make_docs only writes flat top-level files; no test places a .md in a subdirectory or asserts parent-relative link resolution
scripts/check_docs_index.py:84-90 comment + `resolved.relative_to(docs_root)` in try/except ValueError: continue
ABSENCE: no test constructs a link with '../' that escapes docs/ and asserts it is NOT reported as broken
advisory.finding: find_broken_links recurses via rglob('*.md') and resolves each target relative to the linking file's own directory (md.parent / path_part), but every test builds only a single-level docs/ with top-level files. The parent-relative resolution and subdirectory recursion are never exercised — a regression resolving relative to docs_root instead of md.parent would pass all tests while breaking links in real subdirs like docs/adr/.
merged_from: The escape guard that skips links resolving OUTSIDE docs/ (the relative_to(docs_root) try/except, lines 87-90) has no test. A link like ../CONTRIBUTING.md that resolves out of docs/ is intentionally not reported; removing the guard would flag such valid out-of-docs links as broken, but no test would catch that regression.
scenarios: A link in docs/adr/0012.md points to a sibling file via a relative path; a regression that resolves relative to docs/ root instead of the file's dir goes undetected
